data.narrative:
AQT is a Series A quantum computing company founded by Rainer Blatt, Thomas Monz, and Peter Zoller. The quantum computing sector contains 11 identified comparables: 3 public companies (IONQ, RGTI, QBTS) and 8 private firms including Quantinuum, IonQ, PsiQuantum, D-Wave Quantum, and SandboxAQ.

The peer-median method is not applicable to this valuation. While 8 same-sector peers exist, filtering for same-stage, adjacent-stage, or similar-valuation-tier comparables yielded fewer than three datapoints in any narrow cohort, which falls below the minimum threshold needed for reliable triangulation. Applying an all-sector median would introduce unacceptable heterogeneity given the wide variance in maturity, technology approach, and capital efficiency across quantum companies at different development stages.

Without sufficient narrow-peer density, this analysis cannot support a quantitative valuation range through conventional multiples methods. A credible valuation would require either: expansion to broader-stage quantum comparables with explicit adjustments for stage discount; primary diligence on recent Series A fundings in quantum hardware; or focus on cost-of-capital and cash-burn metrics specific to AQT's research roadmap. The scarcity of mature private comparables at Series A stage reflects the emerging nature of the sector and argues for valuation frameworks grounded in technical milestones and funding velocity rather than traditional market multiples.
